findings.title: Landing B1 and B2 introduced two required byte-sets that are not among the fourteen, and every inventory, obligation, later-work item and executability precondition in the artifact remains scoped to 'the fourteen'. The top-level passProperty is therefore false as written for EV-3 and EV-4.
whatWasIntroduced: EV-3.suppliedBy now reads 'FX-5, FX-8, and the named-not-authored R-10 expiry-materialization bytes. Not authored. R-10 is not invented as a fifteenth FX class.' The coordination is additive: the R-10 bytes are required beyond FX-5 and FX-8.
EV-4.suppliedBy now reads 'FX-12, FX-5 cleanup records, and the named-not-authored R-6 process-death bytes. Not authored. R-6 is not invented as a fifteenth FX class.'

Each is a fixture in substance. EV-3 states 'The fixture pins the journal before and after materialization and the PR-5 refusal.' EV-4 states 'The fixture pins the pre-death journal, the recovery start, the post-recovery CLN or residual, and the two bound-origin marks.'

That these bytes fall outside the fourteen is established, not assumed: live v9 FX-5's intent is scoped to file 03's own four revocation conformance positions, so it does not reach R-10; and FX-12 covers duplicate and concurrent revocations, which is R-5, not R-6. The artifact itself holds them outside by saying twice that neither is a new FX identifier.
whatWasNotUpdated: namedCorpusNotAuthored still lists exactly fourteen ids, verified set-equal to live v9 acceptanceEvidenceFixtureClasses.classes.

The top-level passProperty still reads 'Once the fourteen FX implementations exist and are independently pinned, each retained-evidence member's passProperty holds ... Until those bytes exist, this harness cannot be executed and cannot be QUALIFIED.'
proposedLaterWork still routes only 'the fourteen FX implementations' to a later D-000 cycle. No later work is proposed for the R-10 or R-6 bytes.

leftoverDesignRemainingOnDR105 is unchanged at six, and the live permission-leftover-join.v2 scopes OBL-FX-AUTHORING by enumeration — its reason reads 'FX-1, FX-2A, FX-2B, and FX-3..FX-13 are specifications of exact-byte intent, not implementations' — so the R-10 and R-6 bytes fall outside the only authoring obligation on the row, and OBL-FX-AUTHORING's owner is recorded as 'none'.
The token 'fourteen' occurs seven times in the subject and is literal at every occurrence.
findings.operativeBite: The top-level passProperty asserts a sufficiency that the artifact's own member text contradicts: once the fourteen exist, EV-3's expiry limb and EV-4's R-6 limb still have no bytes, so 'each retained-evidence member's passProperty holds' is false for two of the six. The same sentence is the artifact's executability gate, so a harness built to this specification would be declared executable and no longer blocked while precisely the two limbs the blockers were raised about remain unevidenced. Separately, two fixture byte-sets are now required by an accepted-if-accepted specification with no obligation, no owner and no proposed later work naming them, on a row whose leftover inventory this artifact reproduces unchanged.
findings.whyThisIsNotTheBlockersReturning: B1 and B2 are genuinely landed and are not re-charged. EV-3 and EV-4 now state pass predicates that would catch the wall-clock-expiry host and the abandoned-cleanup host, which is what those blockers demanded. The defect here is one level up: the artifact's global pass condition and its corpus inventory were not carried along with the member-level repair.
notRescuedBy: The 'not a fifteenth FX class' disclaimers do not rescue it. They correctly avoid inventing an identifier — R-10 and R-6 are live v9 raceSemantics ids — but declining to name a class does not remove the requirement for bytes, and it is the bytes, not the name, that the inventory and the passProperty are counting.
discipline does not rescue it. 'The fourteen FX classes remain specifications of exact-byte intent; no fixture exists' is true of the fourteen and silent on the two new byte-sets.
OBL-FX-AUTHORING does not rescue it. Its live text enumerates the fourteen, so it does not stretch, and this artifact may not widen an obligation recorded at D-163.
findings.remedyShape: Two honest routes, neither requiring a fifteenth FX class or any fixture bytes. Either carry the repair up — state in the top-level passProperty that the harness becomes executable once the fourteen FX implementations AND the R-10 and R-6 byte-sets exist and are independently pinned, add a proposedLaterWork item routing those two byte-sets to a later independently reviewed act, and record in whatThisCloses that their authoring remains leftover on DR-105 beyond OBL-FX-AUTHORING's fourteen; or, if the intent is that no new bytes are owed, say instead which existing class absorbs each limb and show that its live v9 intent reaches R-10 and R-6, which on these bytes FX-5 and FX-12 do not. This reviewer authors no fixture bytes, mints no FX identifier, and writes no obligation text.
findings.gradeRationale: Graded SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker because the member-level pass predicates are now correct, so no host that violates R-10 or R-6 passes EV-3 or EV-4 as written; the defect is in the artifact's global sufficiency claim and its inventory rather than in a member's test. Graded SHOULD-FIX and not advisory because the top-level passProperty is an operative pass condition and is false as written, and because required bytes are left with no obligation and no owner.

decision.rule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
decision.recommendation: DO-NOT-SEAL. Do not record. Both v1 blockers are cleared at the member level and the SHOULD-FIX is cleared outright; the EV-3, EV-4 and platformCensus work should be kept verbatim. A v3 that carries the repair up to the top-level passProperty, proposedLaterWork and the leftover inventory — or that shows an existing class absorbs each limb — would on these bytes carry no remaining finding known to this reviewer.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: v2 lands all three v1 findings at the member level. EV-3 gains the expiry limb with bytes and a pass predicate faithful to live v9 R-10, closing the wall-clock false-pass path. EV-4 names both bound origins and specifies process death faithfully to R-5 and R-6, closing the abandoned-cleanup false-pass path. platformCensus pins 28 cells against v9's own census method and states the architecture axis as v9's stated invariant. Six failsIf lines were added to guard the repairs. Every mechanical check is clean: subject unmoved at 43c372bd and 0444, six of six cited digests equal live bytes, three recording attributions confirmed in COORD, the six member strings and the claim, waiver, owner and matrix carries all exact against the live DR-G09 row, the fourteen FX ids set-equal to live v9, no proves label inverted, the obligation partition equal to the live D-163 seven-member leftover-design set, file 08 pin equal to live, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, prohibition scan clean. One SHOULD-FIX stands, introduced by the repair: EV-3 and EV-4 now require the R-10 expiry-materialization and R-6 process-death byte-sets, which are not among the fourteen, while namedCorpusNotAuthored, the top-level passProperty, proposedLaterWork and the leftover inventory all remain scoped to the fourteen and the live OBL-FX-AUTHORING enumerates only FX-1 through FX-13. The top-level passProperty's claim that once the fourteen exist each member's passProperty holds is therefore false for two of the six members, and two required byte-sets carry no obligation and no owner.
